description: The bar chart, titled “Recall@10,” visually compares the performance of four different interaction strategies—“- critiquing,” “- scoring,” “- ranking,” and an unlabeled baseline represented by a gray bar—on a metric of recall at the top 10 recommendations. The vertical y-axis is scaled from 0.1 to 0.4 in increments of 0.1, representing the recall value, while the horizontal x-axis lists the four interaction types. The tallest bar, colored orange, corresponds to the “- critiquing” condition and reaches approximately 0.35. The blue bar for “- scoring” is slightly shorter, at about 0.29, while the “- ranking” bar, also blue, is the shortest among the three labeled conditions, at roughly 0.23. The gray bar, positioned first on the left and unlabeled, is the shortest overall, at approximately 0.05, suggesting it represents a baseline or control condition with significantly lower recall. The chart uses distinct colors to differentiate conditions and includes horizontal gridlines to aid in value estimation, with no error bars or additional annotations visible.
